document_check.note: The document is Liu T, Li N, Pu J et al., 'The plasma derived exosomal miRNA-483-5p/502-5p serve as potential MCI biomarkers in aging', Experimental Gerontology 186 (2024) 112355. The first author and year match 'Liu et al. 2024b'. The cited single exosomal miRNA AUC of 0.90 corresponds to miR-483-5p, AUC 0.901 (sensitivity 79.2 %, specificity 100 %), for MCI against age-matched controls.

cited_result: Diagnostic accuracy of plasma exosomal miR-483-5p for MCI against age-matched cognitively normal controls: AUC 0.901, sensitivity 79.2 %, specificity 100 % (24 MCI vs 24 controls; ROC in Fig. 4e).
tool_reason: The cited result is the accuracy (AUC) of a single index biomarker, exosomal miR-483-5p, for classifying MCI against a clinical reference classification, so QUADAS-2 applies.

domains.rationale: MCI cases and controls were sampled separately by known status (two-gate, case-control design), with extreme-group separation on the reference test (MoCA 20.37 vs 26.17). The exclusions removed people with cognition-affecting illness, sensory impairment or poor cooperation, which are harder-to-classify participants. The 'age-matched' controls were about 5 years younger on average. Random selection within groups does not remove the spectrum bias that a case-control design introduces.

signalling.question: 1.1 Was a consecutive or random sample of patients enrolled?
signalling.answer: Probably yes (random within each diagnostic group)
signalling.quote: Recruitment and random selection of 275 participants with signed informed consent were done using a list of register numbers. ... As the biomarker exploration cohort, 24 MCI patients and 24 age-matched controls were chosen at random.

signalling.question: 1.2 Was a case-control design avoided?
signalling.quote: The miRNA-study cohort included 24 MCI patients, 24 age-matched control and 24 supplemented control group below 65 years.

signalling.question: 1.3 Did the study avoid inappropriate exclusions?
signalling.quote: are diagnosed with dementia or other neurodegenerative diseases; diseases that impair cognitive function; suffer from severe mental illness; and are unable to communicate normally, or unable to complete the study due to poor cooperation, hearing impairment, visual impairment, or any other disability ... The exclusion criteria should be as follows: older than 65 years; with a history of illnesses or injuries that have an impact on cognitive function; any inflammation that is acute; people who are unable to converse.

signalling.question: Supplementary: were the controls comparable in age to the cases (spectrum check)?

domains.rationale: No threshold was pre-specified: sensitivity and specificity were read from the ROC analysis on the same 48 participants. ROC curves were constructed for four candidate miRNAs, but results are reported only for the two that differed most. Nothing is said about blinding the assay to group. A 'paired pool plasma' step leaves it unclear whether exosomes were isolated per participant. There is no validation sample, so the AUC of 0.901 is an apparent, optimistic estimate.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were the index test results interpreted without knowledge of the results of the reference standard?
signalling.quote: Searched sections 2.2 to 2.8 and the results for any statement of blinding, masking, coding of samples or operators unaware of group; none found. The assay is quantitative qPCR: 'All results were analyzed using 2⁃△△Ct and were shown as mean ± SEM.'

signalling.question: 2.2 If a threshold was used, was it pre-specified?
signalling.quote: Sensitivity, specificity, and other relevant measures were derived to further evaluate the diagnostic performance.

signalling.question: Supplementary: was the reported marker reported without data-driven selection among candidates?
signalling.quote: Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed using miRNA-132-3p, miR-206, miR-483-5p and miR-502-5p as potential discriminators. ... e. Receiver operating characteristic curves for miR-483-5p and miR-502-5p to discriminate MCI from age-matched control.

signalling.question: Supplementary: was the index test conducted on individual participant samples?
signalling.quote: For uniformity and quantification of exosome isolation, paired pool plasma containing 100 mg protein were prepared.

domains.rationale: MCI was operationalised as a single MoCA cut-off (< 26) inside the Portet 2006 framework. The document names no neuropsychological battery, no clinician consensus and no education adjustment. Education differed strongly between MCI and controls in the survey sample, so a single unadjusted screening cut-off is likely to misclassify some participants. The reference classification was made before the biomarker cohort was drawn, so it was probably interpreted without knowledge of the index test.

signalling.question: 3.1 Is the reference standard likely to correctly classify the target condition?
signalling.quote: Cognitive disorders as evidenced by clinical evaluation (impairment in memory or in another cognitive domain, here, the clinical evaluation shows a score < 26 by MoCA, on the contrary, MoCA ≥26 is considered normal) ... educational level (Pearson χ2 = 52.196，P < 0.001)

signalling.question: 3.2 Were the reference standard results interpreted without knowledge of the results of the index test?
signalling.quote: We started surveying cognitive function in people over 65 years old from September 2019. ... As the biomarker exploration cohort, 24 MCI patients and 24 age-matched controls were chosen at random.

domains.rationale: All participants received the same MoCA-based classification, and the reported sensitivity and specificity (79.2 % and 100 %) are consistent with all 24 + 24 being analysed. The interval between the cognitive assessment and blood collection is not reported.

signalling.question: 4.1 Was there an appropriate interval between index test and reference standard?
signalling.quote: Searched for the date of blood collection relative to the MoCA survey; the only timing statements are 'We started surveying cognitive function in people over 65 years old from September 2019' and 'snap frozen and stored at −80 ◦C within 90 min of blood collection'.

signalling.question: 4.2 Did all patients receive a reference standard?
signalling.quote: Demographic information, MoCA score and concentration of plasma protein were presented in Table 3.

signalling.question: 4.3 Did patients receive the same reference standard?
signalling.quote: 99 participants were found to have MCI based on the criteria of the European Alzheimer's Disease Consortium in 2006.

signalling.question: 4.4 Were all patients included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: From ROC analysis, miR-483-5p showed an AUC of 0.901 (sensitivity 79.2 % and specificity 100 %)

applicability.rationale: Community-dwelling older adults from one mostly urban neighbourhood in northwestern China ('mostly from metropolitan communities', p. 7). Exclusion of people with sensory impairment and cognition-affecting illness narrows the spectrum relative to a screening population.
Plasma exosomal miRNA by ultracentrifugation and qPCR matches a blood-biomarker question, although normalisation used only an external spike-in control (p. 3).
The target condition is MCI defined by a MoCA < 26 cut-off rather than a clinical or neuropsychological consensus diagnosis, so it may not match MCI as defined in other included studies.

overall: High risk of bias (patient selection, index test and reference standard high; flow and timing unclear); applicability concerns unclear.
overall_rationale: The AUC of 0.901 comes from an exploratory two-gate case-control sample of 24 MCI and 24 controls with extreme separation on the reference test. There was no pre-specified threshold, the reported marker was selected from four candidates, and there was no validation sample. The reference classification rests on a single unadjusted MoCA cut-off. Each of these would inflate the apparent accuracy, and three QUADAS-2 domains are high.
